nodes.label: Patient presented with acute shortness of breath and pleuritic chest pain, with significant breathlessness on minimal exertion
30-year-old woman, never-smoker, with medical history of seropositive non-erosive condition diagnosed in 2014; anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide level 261 units·mL−1 and rheumatoid factor 30 IU·mL−1

Previous treatments included hydroxychloroquine and methotrexate for three years until 2017, then leflunomide until 2019; certolizumab was added in 2019 and had been used for 18 months at presentation

Physical examination showed normal pulse, normal blood pressure, normal respiratory rate, and normal oxygen saturations on air at rest, but significant breathlessness on minimal exertion (walking a few steps)
Chest CT shows bilateral small pneumothorax
Chest CT shows cavitary lesions in the lungs
Rheumatoid arthritis-associated necrobiotic nodules (possibly with secondary infection)
Opportunistic pulmonary infection (e.g., fungal or mycobacterial) complicating immunosuppression
No fever was documented at presentation
Sputum culture/BAL and inflammatory markers are not yet available
HRCT pattern and pulmonary function tests are not yet available
Rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease (RA-ILD) with cystic/cavitary changes and secondary pneumothorax
Rheumatoid pleuritis with bilateral small pneumothorax
Combined rheumatoid pleuritis and RA-ILD (overlap pattern)
Biopsy shows necrobiotic granulomas with pleural extension
Bilateral pneumothorax is secondary to ruptured rheumatoid necrobiotic nodules
